Math. Z. 141,199 - 204 (1975)
9 by Springer-Verlag 1975




           The Frattini Subgroup of Locally Free Groups
                                                Samuel Poss


                                               1. I n t r o d u c t i o n
    A group L is locally free (of finite rank m) if every finitely generated subgroup
is contained in a free group (of rank m). We exclude the case m = 1 for then L
would be a subgroup of the rational numbers. There seems to be little known
about locally free groups beyond what is given in [1, 3] and [5]; they are not
simple, their commutator quotient group is torsion free and conversely, any
torsion free abelian group is the commutator quotient of a locally free group,
and, if of finite rank, they must be countable. This paper illustrates a technique
that can sometimes be used to prove that the Frattini subgroup of locally free
groups is trivial.
    Since any locally free group of finite rank m is countable (see [5]), if L has
rank m, then it must be an ascending union of free groups L i of rank m, i = 1, 2 . . . . .
Take as free generators of Li, {Xil, Xi2 . . . . ,xi,,}. Since Li_~cL~, there are
words W/k , such that Xi_ lk : W i _ l k ( X i l , X,i2 ~ . . . , Xim), k : 1, 2 . . . . . m and i = 1, 2 . . . . .
We will illustrate our technique by proving a theorem for certain locally free
groups of rank 2, and then state a result for locally free groups of arbitrary rank,
which may be obtained by generalizing our method. So we assume m = 2 (i.e. L has
rank 2) and take {xi, Yi} to be free generators of L~. If W/k= W / + l k for k = 1, 2
and i = 1, 2 . . . . . then we say L has constant embedding and replace W~I and W/2
by Wand V respectively. Therefore, if Lis free of rank 2 and has constant embedding
(as is assumed for the remainder of this section) then:
      oo
L = ~) L i where each L i has free generators x i and Yl and x i = W ( x i + l , Yi+I),
      1
                                            Yi= V(xi+l, Yi+I)"
   It will sometimes be convenient when discussing the abstract words W and V
to write them as words in symbols A and B, i.e., W ( A , B ) and V(A,B). For
example if

           xi=W(Xi+l,Yi+l)=Xi+l Yi+l                     and        Yi=V(xi+l,Yi+l)=Yi+l Xi+l,
then W(A, B) = A B and V(A, B) = BA. We will without loss of generality assume
that { W(A, B), V(A, B)} is Nielsen reduced (N.R.) in a and B. Familiarity with [4],
pp. 120-125, is assumed in this paper. We are particularly concerned with the
form of the initial and terminal segments of the (freely reduced) words W(A, B)
and V(A, B). We introduce the notation

                                     W ( A , B) = X (A, B) - a (A, B)

to mean that W(A, B) equals
                                   X (a, B) Y(A, 8) Z (a, B)
where X(A, B), Y01, B), and Z(A, B) are freely reduced words in A and B, and no
cancellation occurs between X (A, B) and Y(A, t3) or between Y(A, B) and Z(A, B).
Equivalently, X ( A , B ) and Z(A, B) are disjoint initial and terminal segments
respectively of W(A, B). For example, if

                                W(A, B) = A - 2 B2ABA 2 B - 1

then letting X (A, B) = A- 1 and Z (A, B) = A B - 1,

                                   W(A, B) = A - 1 _ A B - 1.

Letting X(A, B ) = A - 2 B and Z(A, B)=BA2 B -1 we also have

                                 W(A, B ) = A - 2 B - B A 2 B -1.
But it is not valid to choose X (A, B) = A - 2 B2A and Z(A, B) = ABA 2 B - 1 because X
and Z are not disjoint.
    If d is a member of L then for some positive integer k, d is a member of Lj
for .] > k. So for each such j, d has a unique representation, which denote by (d)j,
as a freely reduced word in the generators of L j, xj and Yr" For any pair c, d~L
there is a smallest k such that c, d e L k. If for j > k there is no cancellation between
the terminal segment of (c)j and the initial segment of (d)~ then we say that c is
blocked off from d. Being blocked off is not symmetric.
      I am pleased to thank Gilbert Baumslag for his help and encouragement.



                                  2. A Theorem for Rank 2
    Theorem 1. Let L be a locally free group of rank 2 with constant embedding
given by words W and V. I f W(A, B) and V(A, B) are Nielsen reduced words of the
form
               W(A, B) = A - 1 _ B and V(A, B) = A - 1 _ A B - 1,

then ~L, the Frattini subgroup of L is trivial.
   Proof. In order to prove that for any z~L there is a maximal subgroup ex-
cluding z, it suffices by Zorn's Lemma to exhibit a subgroup H of L excluding z,
which together with z generates L. We d o t h i s first for z=3;1. If S is any subset
of L, ( S ) will denote the subgroup generated by S. We define H n to be the
subgroup generated by the following elements:

mal subgroup of L excluding x2kzxk2, from which it follows that the same is true

   Corollary 1. The locally free group o f rank 2 determined by W (A, B) = A - ~B - ~A B
and V(A, B) = A - 1 B A B - 1 has trivial Frattini subgroup.
      Observe that the group of Corollary 1 is perfect.


                                                   3. Arbitrary Rank
    The method employed to prove Theorem 1 may be extended to prove the
triviality of the Frattini subgroup of certain locally free groups of arbitrary finite
rank, even when the embedding is not constant. We state one such result without
proof. First we must define the simple n-fold commutator [Xx, x2, ..., x~]:

                                             [-X1 , x 2 l ~ _ _ X l l X 2 1 X 1 X 2 '

                                       x 2 .....          : [Ix,,      ...,

      Theorem 2. I f L is the locally free group o f rank m > 3 given by:
           W i - l j ( X i l , Xi 2, ... , X i m ) : [Xij, Xij+ l , ... , Xim, Xi l, Xi 2, . . . , X i j _ l ] i,

then goL= 1.
    While other results like Theorems 1 and 2 may be stated and proved similarly,
there are locally free groups of finite rank for which the embedding L i c L i + 1 ,
seem to preclude our approach. It may be that the triviality of the Frattini subgroup
of locally free groups follows from more general considerations than discussed here.
